items.title: Tanner Bergsma, Waterloo
notes:
T. Bergsma spoke to Council regarding his lived experience with homelessness and stated that there is a housing emergency that requires Council to focus on action. He requested that an amendment to direct staff to engage individuals with lived experience of homelessness—alongside local service providers—to co-develop a clear, time-bound Affordable and Supportive Housing Action Plan by the end of 2025, be added to the recommendation from the Administration and Finance Committee. A copy of his remarks is attached to the minutes.

In response to a question from Council, T. Bergsma stated that he is concerned that the co-creators table is not moving fast enough and stressed the need to work with the people living in encampments.

items.title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee - May 6, 2025
notes:
B. Vrbanovic requested that item five on the summary be taken separately.

Responding to questions, D. Spooner outlined the proposed changes to automated speed enforcement that have been proposed by the province. He noted that because all Regional cameras are published online, well signed at their locations, and the revenue is being used to improve road safety, he is confident that the Region will comply with any changes. He further noted that the Region is charged a daily lease rate for the cameras and that staff can provide more information to Council on the exit clause of the agreement. He stressed that there is a confidential threshold for the cameras to issue a ticket and no one should have a ticket for 1 or 2 km over the limit.

D. Spooner informed Council that staff are currently working on three policy items being that rural speed strategy, a memorandum of understanding with the area municipalities, and a policy to apply the road safety reserve to the areas of most need.

items.title: Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, provided an update on measles, the latest drug alert, and vector borne illnesses. She noted that measles cases continue to increase locally and provincially, largely in the unvaccinated population. Dr. H. Wang provided an overview of the symptoms and who is most vulnerable and explained that the province has expanded the eligibility for receiving the vaccination.

Dr. H. Wang highlighted that a community drug alert was issued due to an increase of overdoses in a short period of time, which can be the result of increased toxicity in the supply. She further noted that as the weather gets warmer, Public Health expects to see an increase in vector borne diseases such as Lyme Disease and West Nile Virus. Dr. H. Wang provided an overview of the work done to address vector borne diseases, including larvicide program.

Responding to questions, Dr. H. Wang stated that the Region’s website is updated in real time with any new measles exposure sites. She explained that measles seems to be spreading among communities that do not support vaccinations, and staff have reached out to those communities and their leadership. Most of the cases are children and Public Health is continuing enforcement of the Immunization of School Pupils Act.

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-CAS-25-008, Code of Conduct Update
notes:
William Short, Regional Clerk, introduced the report, noting that the recommended changes to the Code of Conduct and Council-Staff Relations Policy align with the Municipal Act and represent minor changes to the current documents.

Tim Brubacher, Deputy Clerk, and Chris Fraresso, Legislative Services Specialist, provided a presentation outlining the development of the documents, the relevant provincial legislation, and the notable changes to both the Code of Conduct and Council-Staff Relations Policy.

Responding to questions, C. Fraresso explained that the non-pecuniary interest section provision of the proposed Code of Conduct will allow a Councillor to declare a conflict of interest in instances that are not covered by the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act (MCIA), such as in instances of Committee or Board appointments, hiring, or when a family member or friend that is not covered by the MCIA is involved in a Council decision.

N. Salonen moved to defer a decision on the proposed Code of Conduct to allow for staff to obtain the Integrity Commissioner’s opinion on the broadness of the definition of "conflict of interest" in the proposed Code of Conduct.

motions.item_title: Administration & Finance Committee Summary - May 6, 2025
motions.text: The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows: WHEREAS residents and taxpayers across the region are facing significant financial pressures due to the rising cost of living, including housing, food, fuel, and other essential expenses; AND WHEREAS affordability remains a top concern for many households and businesses within our community; AND WHEREAS ongoing economic uncertainty, including the impact of tariffs and global market instability, continues to place additional strain on local businesses and consumers; AND WHEREAS Regional Council has a responsibility to balance the delivery of essential services with fiscal prudence and affordability for taxpayers; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to prepare and present a draft 2026 budget for all regional services (i.e., excluding police), that limits the increase in the portion of the tax levy which is attributed to all regional services to no more than 5%, while maintaining vital services and seeking efficiencies wherever possible. 2. WHEREAS the United States has imposed tariffs on key Canadian industries, and Canada has implemented counter-tariffs in response; and WHEREAS tariffs are already disrupting local economies across Ontario, jeopardizing jobs, investment, and economic stability in communities of all sizes; and WHEREAS we must protect our most vulnerable residents whose housing supports and services may be negatively impacted by an economic downturn; and WHEREAS infrastructure investments in public transit, Light Rail Transit and improving the electricity grid will simultaneously address the economic uncertainty created by the US imposed tariffs by creating good, local jobs while also addressing the climate crisis; and WHEREAS in times of economic uncertainty, federal and provincial governments have historically stepped up with stimulus investments to support municipalities, create jobs, and maintain economic momentum; and WHEREAS past stimulus initiatives, such as the 2009 Economic Action Plan, which funded 23,000 infrastructure projects across the country in response to the global financial crisis, and the 2020 COVID-19 stimulus plan, which provided critical economic relief during the pandemic, played a critical role in stabilizing local economies and ensuring communities could withstand economic downturns; and WHEREAS municipal governments are uniquely positioned to drive economic recovery by facilitating major infrastructure projects that create well-paying jobs, attract investment, and improve public services for residents; and WHEREAS fast-tracking significant municipal projects as stimulus initiatives would help mitigate the negative economic impacts of US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs while building critical infrastructure that benefits Ontarians for generations; and WHEREAS projects such as housing enabling infrastructure, asset management mitigation and adaptation, transit and transportation infrastructure, affordable housing and supportive housing projects, and other key infrastructure investments that support economic growth, job creation, and sustainable urban development, are ready to serve as engines of economic resilience and community capacity building, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Region of Waterloo Council calls on the federal and provincial governments to introduce comprehensive municipal stimulus strategies to fast-track large-scale investments in infrastructure, housing, transit, state-of-good-repair projects and other critical projects that will help safeguard local economies against the destabilizing effects of US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs; and THAT these stimulus strategies also allow for funding of social housing programs including wrap around services for our most vulnerable residents; and THAT Council urges the federal and provincial governments to work in partnership with municipal associations such as the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and Ontario Big City Mayor, Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) to identify and accelerate key projects (see appendix) to serve as stimulus initiatives, ensuring that economic growth remains centered on protecting the livelihoods and well-being of the people across Waterloo Region. THAT this resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, local MPs, Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus (OBCM), Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), provincial Ministers of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade, Minister of Infrastructure, Minister of Finance, Treasury Board President and Premier Doug Ford and the federal ministerial counterparts when the new federal cabinet is established.
motions.text_html:
The Administration and Finance Committee recommends as follows:

WHEREAS residents and taxpayers across the region are facing significant financial pressures due to the rising cost of living, including housing, food, fuel, and other essential expenses;

AND WHEREAS affordability remains a top concern for many households and businesses within our community;

AND WHEREAS ongoing economic uncertainty, including the impact of tariffs and global market instability, continues to place additional strain on local businesses and consumers;

AND WHEREAS Regional Council has a responsibility to balance the delivery of essential services with fiscal prudence and affordability for taxpayers;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to prepare and present a draft 2026 budget for all regional services (i.e., excluding police), that limits the increase in the portion of the tax levy which is attributed to all regional services to no more than 5%, while maintaining vital services and seeking efficiencies wherever possible.


2.    WHEREAS the United States has imposed tariffs on key Canadian industries, and Canada has implemented counter-tariffs in response; and

WHEREAS tariffs are already disrupting local economies across Ontario, jeopardizing jobs, investment, and economic stability in communities of all sizes; and

WHEREAS we must protect our most vulnerable residents whose housing supports and services may be negatively impacted by an economic downturn; and  

WHEREAS infrastructure investments in public transit, Light Rail Transit and improving the electricity grid will simultaneously address the economic uncertainty created by the US imposed tariffs by creating good, local jobs while also addressing the climate crisis; and

WHEREAS in times of economic uncertainty, federal and provincial governments have historically stepped up with stimulus investments to support municipalities, create jobs, and maintain economic momentum; and

WHEREAS past stimulus initiatives, such as the 2009 Economic Action Plan, which funded 23,000 infrastructure projects across the country in response to the global financial crisis, and the 2020 COVID-19 stimulus plan, which provided critical economic relief during the pandemic, played a critical role in stabilizing local economies and ensuring communities could withstand economic downturns; and

WHEREAS municipal governments are uniquely positioned to drive economic recovery by facilitating major infrastructure projects that create well-paying jobs, attract investment, and improve public services for residents; and

WHEREAS fast-tracking significant municipal projects as stimulus initiatives would help mitigate the negative economic impacts of US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs while building critical infrastructure that benefits Ontarians for generations; and

WHEREAS projects such as housing enabling infrastructure, asset management mitigation and adaptation, transit and transportation infrastructure, affordable housing and supportive housing projects, and other key infrastructure investments that support economic growth, job creation, and sustainable urban development, are ready to serve as engines of economic resilience and community capacity building,

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Region of Waterloo Council calls on the federal and provincial governments to introduce comprehensive municipal stimulus strategies to fast-track large-scale investments in infrastructure, housing, transit, state-of-good-repair projects and other critical projects that will help safeguard local economies against the destabilizing effects of US tariffs and Canadian counter-tariffs; and

THAT these stimulus strategies also allow for funding of social housing programs including wrap around services for our most vulnerable residents; and  

THAT Council urges the federal and provincial governments to work in partnership with municipal associations such as the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and Ontario Big City Mayor, Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), and the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) to identify and accelerate key projects (see appendix) to serve as stimulus initiatives, ensuring that economic growth remains centered on protecting the livelihoods and well-being of the people across Waterloo Region.  

THAT this resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, local MPs, Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus (OBCM), Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), provincial Ministers of Economic Development, Job Creation and Trade, Minister of Infrastructure, Minister of Finance, Treasury Board President and Premier Doug Ford and the federal ministerial counterparts when the new federal cabinet is established.

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo undertakes the following: Declare the lands legally described as Part Lot 34, RCP 1525, being Part 8 on 58R-6243, Kitchener, being part of PIN 22594-0040 (LT) (the “Lands”) surplus to the needs of the Region, as detailed in Report No. PDL-LEG-20, dated May 6, 2025; That the Regional Solicitor be authorized and directed to execute a Land Exchange Agreement on behalf of the Region that includes the transfer of the Lands to the City of Kitchener for a nominal amount, with all terms and conditions subject to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and the Regional Solicitor, in accordance with the Region’s Disposal of Land By-Law (No. 20-042); and Authorize and direct the Regional Solicitor to execute such other documents, to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and the Regional Solicitor, and to carry out the Land Exchange Agreement. WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt; and WHEREAS salt levels in Ontario’s groundwater aquifers, creeks, rivers, and lakes have increasingly worsened since the 1970s, seriously affecting municipal drinking water sources and aquatic life; and WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo, in collaboration with local municipalities, is actively attempting to mitigate salt pollution using existing policies, programs and site design measures that would be significantly more effective with supporting Provincial legislation; and WHEREAS the Ontario and Canadian governments have taken many actions over the past 25 years including setting water quality guidelines, developing voluntary codes of practice, signing the Canada-Ontario Great Lakes Agreement, and holding workshops, yet still the salt problem continues to grow; and WHEREAS numerous situation analyses have recommended salt solutions involving liability protection, contractor certification, government approved Best Management Practices (BMPs) and salt management plans; and WHEREAS increased numbers of slips and falls claims, and other injury/collision claims related to snow and ice, are resulting in salt applicators overusing salt beyond levels considered best practices; and WHEREAS unlimited contractor liability is making it difficult or expensive for snow and ice management contractors to obtain insurance coverage, resulting in contractors leaving the business, thereby making it difficult for municipalities and private owners to find contractors; and WHEREAS the Snow and Ice Management Sector (SMS) of Landscape Ontario is working with the Ontario government to institute a limited liability regime for snow and ice management, including enforceable contractor training/certification and government-approved BMPs for salt application; and WHEREAS many Ontario municipalities have Salt Management Plans, but these often require updating considering improved science and better salt management practices now available. THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to work on a priority basis with key stakeholders to develop limited liability legislation, including enforceable contractor training and a single set of provincially-endorsed standard BMPs for snow and ice management; and The Region of Waterloo urges the province of Ontario to create and fund an expert stakeholder advisory committee to advise the province and municipalities on the best courses of action to protect freshwater ecosystems and drinking water from the impacts of salt pollution; and This resolution be sent to all municipalities in the Regional Municipality of Waterloo, Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), local MPPs, Mayors and Regional Chairs of Ontario (MARCO), Ontario Big City Mayors Caucus (OBCM), Landscape Ontario, Conservation Ontario, the Minister of the Environment Conservation and Parks (MECP), the Minister of Red Tape Reduction, the Attorney General, and Premier Doug Ford. WHEREAS Waterloo Region experienced multiple significant weather events in Winter 2024/2025, resulting in the greatest annual snowfall accumulations since 2008; WHEREAS the Region of Waterloo coordinates winter maintenance of the public right-of-way across multiple operators; WHEREAS timely and appropriate winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is vital for supporting year-round accessibility for all residents and businesses -- particularly those who walk and roll, active transportation users, transit riders, and emergency vehicles; AND WHEREAS responsive and well-coordinated winter maintenance of the public right-of-way is a core municipal service susceptible to variable weather patterns and a changing climate; THEREFORE be it resolved that the Commissioner of Transportation conduct a review of Winter 2024/2025 maintenance operations and prepare a Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the 2026 Plan and Budget process, which: Reviews existing winter maintenance operational standards and agreements to determine how to optimize existing available resources; Investigates and reports on specific issues and coordination opportunities for infrastructure under Regional jurisdiction including but not limited to coordination of snow clearing and overhead ice build-up along the ION LRT corridor and snow clearing of separated cycling tracks and lanes, sidewalks and multi-use trails along Regional Roads, and transit stops; Identifies potential improvements to the Region's winter maintenance programs, policies, and agreements for Council’s consideration; and Establishes a reporting process to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee prior to the Plan and Budget cycle, outlining performance of winter operations from the previous season and insights around operational efforts and future continuous improvements.

  9. WHEREAS road salt is a known toxic substance designated under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act because of tangible threats of serious or irreversible environmental and health damage from road salt; and
